# Muse Hongguo download tools

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

`hongguo_download_info` inspects source availability and declared episode counts. `hongguo_download` accepts several `seriesIds`; omitting `episodes` requests every episode. The default `legacy` mode uses the supplied complete `Hongguo Downloader/app` directory and its original API. Real multi-series acceptance requires successful downloads and media validation; having the source files alone does not establish it.

The downloader requires a declared count and consecutive episode numbers from 1 to N. It resolves up to five exact IDs per unsigned GET to `/reading/bookapi/video_tab/multi_video_model/v1/`, using comma-separated `video_id` and accepting only `data.video_model_data[requestedVideoId].video_model`. Catalog requests retain the local signer. One next batch is prefetched while the current batch downloads; a failed prefetch lets the current verified batch finish before reporting failure. Neither media lookup nor failures switch to previews or regenerate devices.

Each request has a stable `hongguo-*` recovery directory. Every fully decoded episode commits its path, size and SHA256 to `resume-state.json`; signed URLs and encryption material are never persisted. Failure, cancellation and unload stop owned work and remove unfinished `.part` files while retaining validated episodes. Calling again with the same source mode, IDs, episode selection and output directory verifies retained sizes, hashes and MP4 containers, then fetches only missing or changed episodes. Changed manifest contents use a different recovery directory. A crash between a file rename and its journal commit can require downloading that one episode again. Recovery works at completed-episode granularity; incomplete segments do not survive a process restart. Only all requested files passing validation produces a successful `download-manifest.json`. Failure results expose retained and remaining counts, the checkpoint and exact `resume` arguments. Concurrent duplicate requests are refused; a later process can recover an exited writer's lock.

Before source lookup, bounded discovery searches previous successful receipts under the chosen output directory. Complete declared lists with intact requested files can be reused without a source or CDN request. Results retain each actual episode path, which may be inside an earlier download directory. `discoveryTruncated` reports a configured search limit. Standalone hosts must provide the matching `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write` peer dependency.

Large media with a known length, byte-range support and a strong ETag can use parallel ranges. Each segment must match its requested range, length and ETag. A recoverable segment failure cancels and joins all segments before one full-transfer fallback; security refusals and cancellation do not fall back. Connection budgets apply per call. Every new episode checks source lengths, decrypts encrypted tracks through the original offline modules, passes ffprobe and full ffmpeg decoding, and receives a final SHA256 digest. Muse defaults to the initiating workspace's `downloads`. An absolute `outputDir` writes directly under `danger-full-access`; relative paths remain workspace-relative. `read-only` refuses downloads; `workspace-write` and profiles without `sandboxPolicy` retain workspace-only output. Existing parent aliases are canonicalized; child symlinks and replaced output directories are refused. Signed URLs, device fields, cookies, signer output, keys and tokens remain private.

`complete: true` means the downloaded episode numbers cover the source's declared 1–N list. Successful downloads report `fullDecodeChecked: true` and `validationLevel: 'ffprobe-full-decode-sha256'`. Every source mode requires configured ffmpeg and ffprobe; encrypted originals also require the compatible Python runtime and offline modules. Missing runtimes, HLS, unsupported encryption, HTML responses and truncated files fail explicitly. The plugin does not merge or transcode episodes. Desktop keeps the decryption bridge outside ASAR for the external interpreter.

## Configuration

Muse Desktop includes the local Java 17, CPython 3.11, PyCryptodome, signer assets and offline modules. The first source request creates one private device using the original generator and starts the authenticated loopback signer automatically. Standalone profiles can install the tarball using `dsh plugin --profile headless add /absolute/path/muse-hongguo-download-0.1.3.tgz`.

| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceMode` | `legacy` | Original API; `manifest` uses the repair source's authorized catalog; `public` explicitly selects the official public player |
| `legacyAppDir` | Empty | Absolute original `app` directory containing `config.json`, `devices.json`, signer assets and offline modules |
| `signServer` | Empty | Original local signer at `http://127.0.0.1:port`, accessed through `/sign`; an explicit value selects an externally managed signer |
| `signTokenEnv` | `MUSE_HONGGUO_SIGN_TOKEN` | Environment variable name; the token is read only at runtime |
| `pythonExecutable` | Empty | Absolute CPython 3.11 executable with PyCryptodome for the original encrypted-media modules |
| `javaExecutable` | Empty | Absolute Java 17 executable used when `signServer` is omitted |
| `bootstrapDevices` / `deviceBootstrapTimeoutMs` | false / 30000 | Initialize one private device from the pinned original generator / initialization deadline; Desktop enables initialization |
| `signerStartupTimeoutMs` / `signerHeapMb` | 120000 / 1024 | Lazy startup deadline / Java maximum heap in MiB |
| `signerPollIntervalMs` / `signerPortAttempts` | 25 / 4 | Readiness polling interval / attempts after an occupied local port |
| `ffmpegExecutable` / `ffprobeExecutable` | Empty / Empty | Absolute media executables for complete decoding and stream inspection |
| `catalogPath` | Empty | Absolute local JSON catalog using the repair source's `HG_SOURCE_CATALOG` format |
| `outputRoot` | Empty | Explicit standalone-client workspace; Muse uses the initiating session's workspace |
| `mediaUserAgent` | `Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 12)` | Video request identity; original-source media requests omit the website Referer and session credentials |
| `mediaBatchSize` | 5 | Media IDs per video-tab request and download group; 1–5. One next group is prefetched. |
| `mediaConnections` / `mediaConnectionLimit` | 4 / 12 | Per-episode range ceiling / per-call media connection budget; episode concurrency divides the budget. The limit must be at least `concurrency`. |
| `mediaIdleTimeoutMs` | 20000 | Abort a media request after this much network silence; active transfers retain their whole-episode timeout. |
| `mediaSegmentMinBytes` | 2097152 | Minimum bytes per segment; smaller files retain one stream. |
| `mediaRequestIntervalMs` | 6000 | Minimum gap after a media API request completes, shared across concurrent calls and series; queued waits are cancellable and precede the individual request timeout. CDN downloads keep their configured concurrency. |
| `emptySourceCooldownMs` | 120000 | After a valid media model, one empty response per media query may recover once on the same device within the retry budget; all media callers share the cancellable recovery wait. First-use or repeated emptiness stops. |
| `resumeSearchDepth` / `resumeSearchEntries` | 4 / 10000 | Maximum prior-receipt search depth / directory entries; truncation is returned explicitly |
| `retryDelayMs` | 1500 | Delay before bounded transient source or download retries; media-download retries fetch a fresh model for the same episode |
| `mediaHosts` | `*.qznovelvod.com`, `*.douyinvod.com`, `*.idouyinvod.com`, `*.pkoplink.com`, `*.bdcgslb.com`, `*.vegslb.com`, `*.jspcdn.cn`, `*.qrstuvwxyzab.com`, `*.ctydoh.cn` | Allowed source media and observed CDN redirect domains, revalidated on every redirect |
| `mediaPorts` | 443, 9305, 20002 | Allowed HTTPS media ports; pages and source APIs always use 443 |
| `maxSeries` | 10 | Series per call; episode counts come from the complete source catalog, without a separate episode-count cap |
| `concurrency` / `retries` | 3 / 2 | Downloads per batch / transient network retries |
| `requestTimeoutMs` / `downloadTimeoutMs` / `callTimeoutMs` | 20000 / 600000 / 7200000 | Source request / episode download / whole call timeout |
| `maxResponseBytes` / `maxEpisodeBytes` | 8388608 / 1073741824 | Metadata response / episode size limits |
| `mediaProcessGraceMs` | 1000 | Grace period before forcing an owned media process to stop |

The original source must return a declared episode count matching its full list. A missing or mismatched count fails explicitly. Manifest completion covers only the supplied authorized catalog and does not establish Hongguo platform coverage. Public mode must be selected explicitly; its returned video IDs must be valid, unique and match the declared episode count. Download planning uses that actual list without an episode cap. Unavailable episodes fail a full-series request rather than silently substituting previews. Missing original source files likewise never trigger another source mode.

The original runtime uses a generic `config.json`, a private `devices.json`, `devicepool.pyc`, the original signing assets and five offline modules. Muse installs immutable, checksum-checked source resources into its private product data and retains the device across launches. Device initialization failures return a fixed safe error after owned processes stop. It starts `com.hongguo.sign.FqTrace serve` only on first use, with Java 17, UTF-8 process output, a private signing directory, `BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1` and a random per-instance token. Disposal waits for the process and its descendants to stop. An explicit `signServer` retains external local setup, whose `HG_SIGN_TOKEN` must match `signTokenEnv`.

Encrypted tracks use the supplied offline modules through [python/decrypt.py](python/decrypt.py). They require actual CPython 3.11 and PyCryptodome; newer Python versions cannot import these bytecode files. This operation uses the media model's key material and the downloaded file locally, without Android or ADB. The bridge passes private fields only through stdin and suppresses original module diagnostics. Unsupported encryption versions or failed media validation abort the batch.

The bundled patch reads the source, Java and Python paths from `MUSE_HONGGUO_LEGACY_APP_DIR`, `MUSE_HONGGUO_JAVA_PATH` and `MUSE_HONGGUO_PYTHON_PATH`; `MUSE_HONGGUO_BOOTSTRAP_DEVICES=1` enables the original generator for a generic source installation. Desktop supplies these entries. Media paths use `DSH_FFMPEG_PATH` / `DSH_FFPROBE_PATH`, with `FFMPEG_PATH` / `FFPROBE_PATH` as alternatives. The standalone tarball includes both Python bridges but excludes Java, original bytecode, saved device configuration and tokens. Desktop distributes its independently locked runtime; [SOURCE.json](SOURCE.json) records the source fingerprints and owning lock.

## Validation

Run `npm test` and `npm run check` in the plugin directory. Run `python3.11 -I -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` for the bridge; these tests create isolated bytecode fixtures and never load the user's original modules or make platform requests. `node scripts/pack.mjs --out /absolute/output/directory` produces a tarball. Original-source acceptance must download at least two complete declared lists and fully decode every requested episode. Run `npm run test:live` from this workspace with `MUSE_HONGGUO_LIVE_IDS` containing at least two comma-separated real series IDs and the documented source/runtime environment settings; it uses the real managed subprocess provider and writes `live-evidence.json`. Validate retained and newly initialized private device configurations separately: a successful retained device does not establish new-install availability. Initialization creates local fields; it does not verify platform acceptance. Public previews and authorized catalogs must be recorded separately from original-source multi-series acceptance.

## Catalog and source failures

`hongguo_download_info` does not request video models or download files. `completeCatalog` checks the declared count against the list; `mediaUrlsVerified` remains false and `fullSeriesAvailable` is null unless a public preview explicitly excludes part of the series, when it is false. `accessibleEpisodeCount` is the public player's declared open count, or null for other modes. Only a successful `hongguo_download` receipt verifies downloaded episodes and full decoding.

Source responses validate `code`, `Code` and `BaseResp.StatusCode` together. A nonzero code cannot be hidden by another zero. Failures expose only the numeric `upstreamCode`, `sourceStage` (`catalog`, `video_model`, or `source_api`) and `retryable: false`. Raw source messages, device values, signer output and media URLs stay private. Connection failures, truncated source responses, HTTP 429 and HTTP 5xx use the bounded retry budget on the retained device. First-use or repeated empty responses, authorization and unknown business failures stop without retrying or rotating the device. After a valid media model, an empty media response may recover once on the same device after `emptySourceCooldownMs`, within the retry budget. The active batch keeps its already downloaded files during that cancellable wait; another empty response ends the call while retaining validated episodes. A single media request timeout returns `source_timeout` after the cancellable queue has finished. Explicit risk or rate-limit messages use the configured bounded retry budget; exhausted calls must not be immediately resubmitted. A platform error does not establish that a title is unavailable; do not turn it into a missing-media claim or immediately repeat the exhausted download.

An HTTP 200 response with no body returns `empty_source_response`; a nonempty body that cannot be parsed returns `platform_json`. Both retain `sourceStage`, `httpStatus`, `responseBytes` and `retryable: false` without exposing response bytes. Terminal empty-response failures stop repeated downloads; retain the private device configuration for diagnosis. The recovery wait does not cool the computer or establish provider throttling. An empty response does not establish a platform-wide outage or authorize automatic device regeneration or preview substitution. A manually restored local configuration is read when a new client starts; an existing client retains its cached configuration until disposal.

Live installed-download qualification is documented in the [Desktop verification reference](../../../apps/desktop/tests/README.md).
